research_question: Do elections (as a proxy for political uncertainty) reduce capital inflows to emerging markets?
sample: 38 emerging markets (China excluded: no DPI/NELDA election dates)
dependent_variables: Gross private capital inflows (official OI liabilities and SDR allocations removed), scaled by HP-filtered trend GDP; also by type
main_explanatory_variables: Election-quarter dummy (exec-relevant: legislative in parliamentary, executive in presidential systems; DPI2020 + NELDA); 1–2 and 3–4 quarter leads/lags; ICRG political stability; WGI
methodology: Panel FE (country FE, country trends; time FE in robustness); push-pull controls
identification: Election timing; pre-determined vs off-cycle elections distinguished; no causal design beyond timing
main_findings: Election quarters associated with lower gross private inflows; no significant run-up decline; effects up to two quarters after; bottom-quartile ICRG stability ≈ −1.25% of trend GDP (≈28% of pre-election inflows); stronger institutions mitigate
limitations: EM-only; ends 2020; ICRG is proprietary; trend-GDP scaling
relevance: Benchmark for H1, H2, H6; our post-hoc analysis aligns window and outcome to it
replication_potential: Partially replicable with public BOP + election dates; ICRG not public

research_question: Does political (election) uncertainty affect US firms' cross-border flows of capital?
sample: FDI flows from US companies to foreign affiliates across host countries
dependent_variables: FDI flows from US parents to affiliates; foreign portfolio flows (comparison)
main_findings: FDI falls before elections and recovers after; no comparable cycle in portfolio flows; smaller variation with higher institutional quality (per FEDS 2013-64 abstract)
limitations: US source country only; bilateral affiliate flows rather than total BOP flows
relevance: Motivates H1 timing and H3 (irreversible FDI vs reversible portfolio flows) and H2

research_question: Do corporate investment cycles follow national elections?
main_findings: Investment falls 4.8% in election years vs non-election years; evidence consistent with uncertainty channel

research_question: Do elections with high policy uncertainty produce pre-election declines in investment?
main_findings: Reverse electoral business cycles exist when polarisation and competitiveness are high
relevance: Suggests election effects are conditional, supporting heterogeneous effects in H2/H6

research_question: Is political uncertainty priced in option markets?
main_explanatory_variables: National elections and global summits within option lives
identification: Timing of elections relative to option maturity
main_findings: Options spanning political events are more expensive; effects spill over across countries
relevance: Supports elections as dated political-uncertainty events (financial-market response outcome)

research_question: Why doesn't capital flow from rich to poor countries?
main_findings: Low institutional quality is the leading explanation of the Lucas paradox
relevance: Motivates institutional moderation (H2) and between-country Mundlak analysis

research_question: Do democratic regimes attract more FDI?
main_findings: Democracies attract more FDI, across and within countries
relevance: Regime type vs election uncertainty distinction (Rule 6)

research_question: Does democracy promote or hinder FDI to developing countries?
main_findings: Competing effects; net effect depends on property-rights protection vs democratic constraints
relevance: Institutions vs regime distinction; H2 moderators

research_question: What drives capital flows to EMs? (survey)
main_findings: Push factors matter most for portfolio flows; pull factors matter for all components, most for banking flows
relevance: Framework for controls and component-specific hypotheses (H3, H5)

research_question: Are capital flows fickle, by type?
main_findings: FDI more stable than non-FDI; portfolio debt and bank flows most volatile; FDI driven by pull, portfolio by push factors

research_question: How do gross flows differ by domestic sector?
dependent_variables: Gross flows by banks, corporates, sovereigns
main_findings: Inflow-outflow co-movement driven by banks; sovereign flows often offset private flows, especially in EMs
relevance: Justifies separating private from official flows (post-hoc analysis) and the gross inflow/outflow retrenchment pattern

research_question: What drives extreme gross capital-flow episodes (surges, stops, flight, retrenchment)?
main_findings: Global factors, especially global risk, are central to episodes; domestic factors matter less
relevance: Sudden-stop definition used in R1; motivates H5

research_question: Is there a global financial cycle constraining monetary independence?
main_findings: A global financial cycle co-moving with VIX drives flows and credit
